1: # Fluent name registry
2: 
3: Canonical list of every `fluent` name ever introduced into
4: `state/fluents.json`, one line each: name, then a short description of
5: the concept it represents. The norm-implementer checks this before naming
6: a new fluent — CodeGraph indexes code structure, not string
7: literals, so it won't reliably catch a near-duplicate name for a concept
8: that already exists under a different name. Reuse an existing name for an
9: existing concept; only add an entry here when a round introduces a
10: genuinely new one, as part of that same round's edit.
11: 
12: | fluent name | represents |
13: |---|---|
14: | `fisher` | The base role every agent holds from round 0 — eligibility to act as a fisher. Assigned via `assign_role()`, never carries `narration` (deliberately invisible to the notice renderer — see CLAUDE.md's "Fluent narration and visibility"). |
15: | `dead` | Permanent — an agent whose running food balance (`runtime["payoff"]`) went negative in `actions/handlers/harvest.py`. Written by the fixed survival mechanic (`engine/physics.py`'s `apply_consumption()`/`is_dead()`), not a norm-implementer mechanism; never terminated once set. Always `visibility="public"`, narration in third person (not "you") since the same string is read by both the affected agent and everyone else it's visible to. |
16: | `rule_active` | The queryable *history* of which `rule_types` entry was actually enforced, for which action, and for how long — `holder="community"`, `args={"action": "<action_name>", "type": "<the rule_types key>"}` (a dict, not a list — the one deliberate exception to every other fluent's `args` shape, since a rule type has no single agent to key off, and needs both action+type to be unique since a type_name is only unique within its own action's rule directory). Opened via `set_fact()` the same round `state/config.json`'s `"rules"[action_name]` list activates a type, closed via `end_fact()` the round it's removed/replaced (or automatically, on natural lifecycle expiry — see `engine.institution.rules.tick_rule_lifecycles()`) — this is what actually answers "was this rule in force during round N for this action," which `state/institution.json`'s `rule_types` catalog (static: what types *exist*) deliberately does not track. Never confuse the two: `rule_types` changes only when a genuinely new shape is invented; `rule_active` changes every time a round's config activates, deactivates, or a rule's own duration expires one. |

13: def current_holder(fluents, role_name, round_number):
14:     """The agent_id currently holding role_name, or None if unassigned.
15:     Unlike role_holder() above (which checks whether one *specific* agent
16:     holds a role — the question a fisher's own prompt needs to answer
17:     about itself), this answers "who holds it" without knowing who to ask
18:     first — the lookup an action needs when its own institution.json
19:     `actor_role` names a role but the specific agent rotates over rounds.
20:     Deliberately never cached anywhere (not in institution.json, not on
21:     any object) — this function, called fresh each time, is the single
22:     place "who currently holds this role" gets answered, so a rotation
23:     can never leave a second, stale answer sitting somewhere else. Relies
24:     on the same exclusivity every role fluent already has: one open
25:     record per role name at a time (set_fact()'s own termination-on-write
26:     behavior enforces this for role fluents the same as any other)."""
27:     for record in fluents:
28:         if (
29:             record["fluent"] == role_name
30:             and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
31:             and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
32:         ):
33:             return record["holder"]
34:     return None
35:

37: def set_fact(
38:     fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
39:     narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
40: ):
41:     """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
42:     exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
43:     the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
44:     non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
45:     tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
46:     "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.
47: 
48:     `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
49:     (the same convention actions/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
50:     `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
51:     record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
52:     how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
53:     holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
54:     migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
55:     `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
56:     agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
57:     `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
58:     monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
59:     public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
60:     agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.
61: 
62:     Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
63:     layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
64:     picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
65:     entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
66:     fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
67:     `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).
68:     """
69:     for record in fluents:
70:         if (
71:             record["fluent"] == fluent_name
72:             and record["args"] == args
73:             and record["terminated_round"] is None
74:         ):
75:             record["terminated_round"] = round_number
76:     record = {
77:         "fluent": fluent_name,
78:         "args": args,
79:         "holder": holder,
80:         "initiated_round": round_number,
81:         "terminated_round": None,
82:     }
83:     if narration is not None:
84:         record["narration"] = narration
85:         record["visibility"] = visibility
86:         record["event_type"] = event_type
87:     fluents.append(record)
88:     return fluents
89:

91: def end_fact(
92:     fluents, fluent_name, args, round_number,
93:     narration=None, visibility=None, event_type="fact_ended",
94: ):
95:     """Terminate the open record for (fluent_name, args), if any, without
96:     opening a replacement — e.g. a ban that's been served in full. Pass
97:     `narration` to describe the closing event itself (e.g. "Your ban has
98:     been lifted.") — same rules as `set_fact()`: reaches prompt (for
99:     exactly the round it closes, via `visible_facts()`) and memory
100:     automatically. `visibility` defaults to the record's own opening
101:     `visibility` if not given; only meaningful when `narration` is set."""
102:     for record in fluents:
103:         if (
104:             record["fluent"] == fluent_name
105:             and record["args"] == args
106:             and record["terminated_round"] is None
107:         ):
108:             record["terminated_round"] = round_number
109:             if narration is not None:
110:                 record["end_narration"] = narration
111:                 record["end_visibility"] = (
112:                     visibility if visibility is not None else record.get("visibility", "agent_only")
113:                 )
114:                 record["end_event_type"] = event_type
115:     return fluents
116: 
117: 
118: def _visible_to(agent_id, holder, visibility):
119:     return visibility == "public" or holder == agent_id
120: 
121: 
122: def visible_facts(fluents, agent_id, round_number):
123:     """Every fluent record with something narrated for right now and
124:     visible to agent_id — either public, or held by agent_id itself. Two
125:     cases: a currently-holdsAt record's opening `narration` (visible for
126:     as long as the fact stays open), and a record that closed exactly this
127:     round, surfaced via its `end_narration` for that one round only (the
128:     two are mutually exclusive per record: a record can't be both
129:     currently-open and closed-this-round). Used by the engine's prompt
130:     renderer to build an agent's "what's currently true" section; never
131:     interprets a raw value itself, only surfaces narration the mechanism
132:     that wrote the fact already authored."""
133:     results = []
134:     for record in fluents:
135:         if (
136:             record.get("narration")
137:             and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("visibility"))
138:             and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
139:             and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
140:         ):
141:             results.append(record)
142:         elif (
143:             record.get("terminated_round") == round_number
144:             and record.get("end_narration")
145:             and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility"))
146:         ):
147:             results.append({**record, "narration": record["end_narration"]})
148:     return results
149:

151: def fact_memory_events(fluents, round_number):
152:     """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
153:     this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the
154:     shape `actions/*.py`'s `memory_writes()` already returns:
155:     `{event_type, text, agent_id, group_id}`). The caller
156:     (`engine/simulate.py`) turns these into actual `write_episode()` calls,
157:     once per round after all of that round's actions have run — not once
158:     per action, since a fact set by an early action would otherwise still
159:     read as "newly opened" to a later action's own call and get logged
160:     twice."""
161:     events = []
162:     for record in fluents:
163:         if record.get("initiated_round") == round_number and record.get("narration"):
164:             events.append(_memory_spec(
165:                 record["holder"], record.get("visibility", "agent_only"),
166:                 record.get("event_type", "fact_initiated"), record["narration"],
167:             ))
168:         if record.get("terminated_round") == round_number and record.get("end_narration"):
169:             events.append(_memory_spec(
170:                 record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility", "agent_only"),
171:                 record.get("end_event_type", "fact_ended"), record["end_narration"],
172:             ))
173:     return events
174: 
175: 
176: def _memory_spec(holder, visibility, event_type, text):
177:     group_id = "community" if visibility == "public" else holder
178:     agent_id = None if holder == "community" else holder
179:     return {"event_type": event_type, "text": text, "agent_id": agent_id, "group_id": group_id}
180:

182: def assign_role(
183:     role_name, agent_id, fluents, round_number, args=None,
184:     exclusive=False, narration=None, visibility="public", event_type="fact_initiated",
185: ):
186:     """The default `args=None` (-> `[agent_id]`) is correct only for a role
187:     every eligible agent holds *simultaneously and independently* (e.g.
188:     "fisher" — one open record per agent, all coexisting on purpose).
189: 
190:     For a role only one agent holds *at a time* (a rotating recorder,
191:     steward, monitor), pass `exclusive=True` instead of trying to get
192:     `args` right yourself — set_fact()'s own termination logic only closes
193:     a previous record when `(fluent_name, args)` matches exactly, so a
194:     plain `args=[agent_id]` for an exclusive role means each new holder's
195:     assignment uses different args than the last, never terminates the
196:     previous holder's record, and leaves multiple simultaneously-"open"
197:     holders for the same role — confirmed directly: `current_holder()`
198:     then returns whichever one happens to appear first in `fluents`,
199:     silently wrong the instant a rotation happens. `exclusive=True` forces
200:     a fixed `args=[]` regardless of whatever `args` was passed, making
201:     that mistake structurally unreachable through this parameter rather
202:     than something the caller has to remember to get right.
203: 
204:     `narration`/`visibility`/`event_type` let a role grant also be a
205:     visible, memory-worthy event (e.g. "Kai has become the pot keeper") —
206:     same contract as `set_fact()`, since this is just its role-shaped
207:     convenience wrapper; previously always silent (`narration=None`)."""
208:     resolved_args = [] if exclusive else (args if args is not None else [agent_id])

def set_fact(
    fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
    narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
):
    """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
    exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
    the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
    non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
    tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
    "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.

    `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
    (the same convention actions/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
    `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
    record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
    how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
    holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
    migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
    `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
    agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
    `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
    monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
    public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
    agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.

    Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
    layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
    picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
    entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
    fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
    `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).

            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
            and record["args"] == args
            and record["terminated_round"] is None

        "fluent": fluent_name,
        "args": args,
        "holder": holder,
        "initiated_round": round_number,
        "terminated_round": None,
    }
    if narration is not None:
        record["narration"] = narration
        record["visibility"] = visibility
        record["event_type"] = event_type

    fluents, fluent_name, args, round_number,

    opening a replacement — e.g. a ban that's been served in full. Pass
    `narration` to describe the closing event itself (e.g. "Your ban has
    been lifted.") — same rules as `set_fact()`: reaches prompt (for
    exactly the round it closes, via `visible_facts()`) and memory
    automatically. `visibility` defaults to the record's own opening
    `visibility` if not given; only meaningful when `narration` is set."""

            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
            and record["args"] == args
            and record["terminated_round"] is None

                record["end_visibility"] = (
                    visibility if visibility is not None else record.get("visibility", "agent_only")

    return visibility == "public" or holder == agent_id


def visible_facts(fluents, agent_id, round_number):
    """Every fluent record with something narrated for right now and
    visible to agent_id — either public, or held by agent_id itself. Two
    cases: a currently-holdsAt record's opening `narration` (visible for
    as long as the fact stays open), and a record that closed exactly this
    round, surfaced via its `end_narration` for that one round only (the
    two are mutually exclusive per record: a record can't be both
    currently-open and closed-this-round). Used by the engine's prompt
    renderer to build an agent's "what's currently true" section; never
    interprets a raw value itself, only surfaces narration the mechanism
    that wrote the fact already authored."""
    results = []
    for record in fluents:
        if (
            record.get("narration")
            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("visibility"))
            and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
            and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
        ):
            results.append(record)
        elif (
            record.get("terminated_round") == round_number
            and record.get("end_narration")
            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility"))

def fact_memory_events(fluents, round_number):
    """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
    this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the
    shape `actions/*.py`'s `memory_writes()` already returns:
    `{event_type, text, agent_id, group_id}`). The caller
    (`engine/simulate.py`) turns these into actual `write_episode()` calls,
    once per round after all of that round's actions have run — not once
    per action, since a fact set by an early action would otherwise still
    read as "newly opened" to a later action's own call and get logged
    twice."""
    events = []
    for record in fluents:
        if record.get("initiated_round") == round_number and record.get("narration"):
            events.append(_memory_spec(
                record["holder"], record.get("visibility", "agent_only"),
                record.get("event_type", "fact_initiated"), record["narration"],

**Existing institution** (from `state/institution.json`):

- Role: `fisher` (non‑exclusive, every alive agent holds it).

**Norm ( round 1 )** – Policy & Operationalization  
1. Limit each fisher’s catch per trip to the lower of 4 kg or 10 % of the lake’s current stock.  
2. Any excess must be handed to **community storage** (a shared ledger).  
3. Excess hand‑over is recorded in the ledger by the **appointed fish keeper**.  
4. The ledger is submitted daily to the **council**, which records violations and updates a **ban register**.  
5. Ban register is public; a fisher named on it is barred for 7 days, after which the ban expires automatically.  
6. Council meets weekly to verify bans have expired and may adjust limits when lake‑stock changes.  

**Extracted atomic requirements** (actor + verb + object):  

| # | Requirement (actor‑verb‑object) | Type |
|---|--------------------------------|------|
|1|Fisher *records* catch per trip (kg) | Action‑level (harvest) – deterministic |
|2|System *calculates* limit = min(4 kg, 10 % stock) | Deterministic (Level 1) |
|3|Fisher *hands* excess to community storage | Action‑level (new rule on harvest) – deterministic |
|4|Fish‑keeper *logs* excess in ledger | New **institutional object** (ledger) – Level 2 |
|5|Council *receives* daily ledger submission | Action `propose`‑like (new action) – Level 2 |
|6|Council *records* violations in ban register | New **institutional object** (ban register) – Level 2 |
|7|Ban register *bars* fisher for 7 days | Fluent `ban` (standard ban fluent) – Level 1 |
|8|Ban automatically *expires* after 7 days | Fluent lifecycle – Level 1 |
|9|Council *reviews* ledger weekly, *adjusts* limits | New **action** (weekly council meeting) – Level 2 |

**Routing & Levels** (per Section 3 decision‑granularity rule):  

- Requirements 1, 2, 3 are deterministic constraints on the existing `harvest` action → **Level 3 rule** under `actions/rules/harvest/`.  
- Requirement 4 needs a shared institutional object → **Level 2 object type** `community_storage` (object type + instance).  
- Requirement 5 is a daily submission of the ledger; the ledger already exists, but a *daily reporting* step is needed → **Level 2 new action** `submit_ledger` (generic_agent_decision).  
- Requirement 6 (record violations) uses the same ban fluent, no new object needed – the ban fluents already exist via `set_fact`/`end_fact`.  
- Requirement 7 and 8 are handled by the existing ban fluent (`set_fact` creates a 7‑round ban, `end_fact` ends it automatically). → **Level 1 config only** (no new code).  
- Requirement 9 (weekly council meeting) is a new action `council_meeting` (generic_agent_decision) that may adjust limits via config change – **Level 2**.  

No new roles are strictly required because the “appointed fish keeper” and “council” can be modelled as agents holding existing roles (or as participants of the new actions). The norm does not specify exclusive rotating roles, so we keep them as ordinary participants.  

**Verification plan** (Section 15): each new rule or action will have a corresponding `tests/norm_checks/` test exercising the behavior, plus existing regression tests will still pass.

**2. Code Implementer (Sections 6‑16)**  

### 2.1 New rule for harvest – excess handling & ban
File **`actions/rules/harvest/catch_limit.py`** (Level 3) added.

- Reads current stock from `ctx.state["runtime"]["stock_kg"]`.  
- Computes limit = `min(4.0, 0.10 * stock)`.  
- If excess > 0, deposits excess into `community_storage` object, creates a 7‑round ban fluent via `set_fact` (using `roles.roles.set_fact`) with public narration, and records a note for the fisher.  

### 2.2 New institutional object type – community storage
File **`state/object_types/community_storage.json`** created (Level 2).

```python
1	"""Fixed simulation physics — never editable by the norm-implementer,
2	regardless of what any norm asks for. Ported directly from Gupta et al.'s
3	CPR-game codebase (Codes/Gupta/CPRG_fishing, branch origin/hiromu/llm-norm,
4	ostrom3/Agent.py and Model.py), not this project's own design — a norm can
5	change caps, deposits, bans, and schedules (all implementer-owned, in
6	actions/rules/ and actions/), but the underlying catch equation, regrowth
7	rate, and survival economics below are the fixed rules of the world those
8	choices play out against, not something a community vote should be able
9	to rewrite.
10	
11	Lives under engine/ specifically so it's outside the norm-implementer's
12	permission.edit allowlist (actions/rules/*/*, actions/*, prompts/*, plus a
13	few named files) by construction, the same way engine/simulate.py and
14	engine/llm_agents.py already are. The rate constants below live here for
15	the same reason the equations do, not in state/config.json (which the
16	norm-implementer can freely edit) — a fixed formula reading a
17	norm-implementer-editable rate is exactly as rewritable as the formula
18	itself would be.
19	
20	`available_stock()` moved in from the old `mechanisms/stock_check.py`
21	(2026-09-09, when `mechanisms/` was renamed to `roles/` and reserved for
22	role/fluent code only) — it's a trivial one-line accessor, but it's fixed
23	protected infrastructure exactly like everything else here, not
24	role-related, so it belongs next to the physics it reads alongside.
25	"""
26	
27	HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY = 0.05  # catchability coefficient q in catch_from_effort()
28	GROWTH_RATE = 0.2  # logistic growth rate in apply_regrowth()
29	CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG = 300  # lake's ceiling, also its starting stock
30	CONSUMPTION_KG = 1.0  # fixed per-round cost every fisher owes just to get by
31	
32	
33	def catch_from_effort(effort, stock_kg):
34	    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
35	    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
36	    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
37	    is their catchability coefficient q."""
38	    return effort * stock_kg * HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
39	
40	
41	def apply_regrowth(stock_kg):
42	    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
43	    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
44	    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
45	    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
46	    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
47	    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
48	    return min(grown, CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
49	
50	
51	def apply_consumption(payoff, harvested_kg):
52	    """Running per-agent balance: this trip's catch in, the fixed
53	    consumption cost out — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest():
54	    self.payoff += harvest_amount; self.payoff -= self.model.consumption.
55	    Unlike catch/regrowth this isn't about the lake at all — it's whether
56	    a fisher can keep feeding themselves from what they bring in."""
57	    return payoff + harvested_kg - CONSUMPTION_KG
58	
59	
60	def is_dead(payoff):
61	    """Matches Gupta et al.'s `if self.payoff < 0: self.dead = True` —
62	    permanent once true; nothing in this project ever resurrects an agent."""
63	    return payoff < 0
64	
65	
66	def alive_agent_ids(agents, runtime):
67	    """The agent_id iteration order every action should use, not
68	    state["agents"] directly — excludes anyone in runtime["dead_agents"].
69	    One shared helper so death exclusion can't be forgotten by an action
70	    rewrite the way a hand-rolled check per action could be."""
71	    dead = set(runtime.get("dead_agents", []))
72	    return [agent_id for agent_id in agents if agent_id not in dead]
73	
74	
75	def available_stock(runtime):
76	    return runtime["stock_kg"]
```

1: Policy: No fisher may take more than 4 kg per trip or 10 % of the lake’s current stock, whichever is lower; any excess must be handed to community storage and a violation incurs a one‑week ban.
2: 
3: Operationalization: 1. Dawn: every fisher casts a small standard sample net, counts fish, and records the number in the shared ledger.
4: 2. The council multiplies that count by the lake‑to‑net area ratio to estimate daily stock, calculates 10 % of that stock, and posts the 10 % limit, the 4 kg bag size, and the daily stock estimate on the ledger and community bulletin.
5: 3. Before setting out, each fisher marks their gear with the 4 kg bag or the 10 % limit, weighs their haul, and records the total catch and any excess in the ledger.
6: 4. If the haul exceeds the lower of 4 kg or 10 %, the fisher hands the excess bag to the appointed fish keeper; the fish keeper logs the excess weight in the ledger under the fisher’s name and the date.
7: 5. The ledger is submitted daily to the council; the council reviews it each day, records any violations, and updates the ban register.
8: 6. The ban register is kept on a public board in the storage shed and in the ledger; any fisher named on it is barred from setting out for seven consecutive days, after which the ban expires automatically.
9: 7. The council holds a weekly meeting to review the ledger, verify that bans have expired, and adjust the 10 % limit or 4 kg bag size if the lake stock estimate has changed.

```python
152	    """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
153	    this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the
154	    shape `actions/*.py`'s `memory_writes()` already returns:

156	    (`engine/simulate.py`) turns these into actual `write_episode()` calls,
157	    once per round after all of that round's actions have run — not once
158	    per action, since a fact set by an early action would otherwise still
159	    read as "newly opened" to a later action's own call and get logged
160	    twice."""

167	            ))

169	            events.append(_memory_spec(

193	    a previous record when `(fluent_name, args)` matches exactly, so a
194	    plain `args=[agent_id]` for an exclusive role means each new holder's
195	    assignment uses different args than the last, never terminates the
196	    previous holder's record, and leaves multiple simultaneously-"open"
197	    holders for the same role — confirmed directly: `current_holder()`
198	    then returns whichever one happens to appear first in `fluents`,
199	    silently wrong the instant a rotation happens. `exclusive=True` forces
200	    a fixed `args=[]` regardless of whatever `args` was passed, making
201	    that mistake structurally unreachable through this parameter rather
```

import engine.institution.rules as rules_module
import engine.llm_agents as llm_agents_module
import actions.handlers.harvest as harvest_handler
from engine.institution.context import ActionContext
from engine.institution.rules import Rule
from engine.physics import apply_consumption, apply_regrowth, catch_from_effort

# The deterministic proof that harvest's own physics, plus the generic
# per-agent rule hooks (is_eligible/after_agent) every action now exposes,
# produce the exact numbers they always have — with no rule configured at
# all, and with one actually attached.

EFFORTS = {"agent_0": 0.5, "agent_1": 0.2}
SPEC = {"name": "harvest"}


def _fake_call_fisher_agent(agent_id, round_number, action_name, **fields):
    return {"effort": EFFORTS[agent_id], "reasoning": "test"}


def _state(rules_config=None):
    return {
        "config": {"rules": {"harvest": rules_config or []}},
        "fluents": [],
        "runtime": {"stock_kg": 300.0, "rounds": []},
        "agents": {
            "agent_0": {"name": "Kai", "personality_traits": ""},
            "agent_1": {"name": "Mara", "personality_traits": ""},
        },
        "round_number": 1,
    }


def _run(state):
    ctx = ActionContext.build(SPEC, state, state["round_number"])
    return harvest_handler.run(ctx)


def test_baseline_empty_rules_matches_hand_computed_physics(monkeypatch):
    monkeypatch.setattr(llm_agents_module, "call_fisher_agent", _fake_call_fisher_agent)
    state = _state()

    record = _run(state)

    raw_0 = catch_from_effort(0.5, 300.0)
    raw_1 = catch_from_effort(0.2, 300.0)
    assert record["agents"]["agent_0"]["harvested_kg"] == pytest.approx(raw_0)

```python
28	GROWTH_RATE = 0.2  # logistic growth rate in apply_regrowth()

34	    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
35	    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
36	    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
37	    is their catchability coefficient q."""
38	    return effort * stock_kg * HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY

42	    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
43	    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
44	    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
45	    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
46	    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
47	    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
48	    return min(grown, CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)

57	    return payoff + harvested_kg - CONSUMPTION_KG
```

```python
96	    opening a replacement — e.g. a ban that's been served in full. Pass
97	    `narration` to describe the closing event itself (e.g. "Your ban has
98	    been lifted.") — same rules as `set_fact()`: reaches prompt (for

100	    automatically. `visibility` defaults to the record's own opening
101	    `visibility` if not given; only meaningful when `narration` is set."""

103	        if (
104	            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
105	            and record["args"] == args
106	            and record["terminated_round"] is None
107	        ):
108	            record["terminated_round"] = round_number
109	            if narration is not None:
110	                record["end_narration"] = narration
111	                record["end_visibility"] = (

118	def _visible_to(agent_id, holder, visibility):
119	    return visibility == "public" or holder == agent_id

122	def visible_facts(fluents, agent_id, round_number):
123	    """Every fluent record with something narrated for right now and
124	    visible to agent_id — either public, or held by agent_id itself. Two
125	    cases: a currently-holdsAt record's opening `narration` (visible for
126	    as long as the fact stays open), and a record that closed exactly this
127	    round, surfaced via its `end_narration` for that one round only (the
128	    two are mutually exclusive per record: a record can't be both
129	    currently-open and closed-this-round). Used by the engine's prompt
130	    renderer to build an agent's "what's currently true" section; never
131	    interprets a raw value itself, only surfaces narration the mechanism
132	    that wrote the fact already authored."""

134	    for record in fluents:

136	            record.get("narration")
137	            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("visibility"))
138	            and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
139	            and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
140	        ):
141	            results.append(record)
142	        elif (
143	            record.get("terminated_round") == round_number
144	            and record.get("end_narration")
145	            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility"))
146	        ):
147	            results.append({**record, "narration": record["end_narration"]})
148	    return results

151	def fact_memory_events(fluents, round_number):
152	    """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
153	    this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the
154	    shape `actions/*.py`'s `memory_writes()` already returns:
155	    `{event_type, text, agent_id, group_id}`). The caller
156	    (`engine/simulate.py`) turns these into actual `write_episode()` calls,
157	    once per round after all of that round's actions have run — not once
158	    per action, since a fact set by an early action would otherwise still
159	    read as "newly opened" to a later action's own call and get logged
160	    twice."""
161	    events = []
162	    for record in fluents:
163	        if record.get("initiated_round") == round_number and record.get("narration"):
164	            events.append(_memory_spec(
165	                record["holder"], record.get("visibility", "agent_only"),
166	                record.get("event_type", "fact_initiated"), record["narration"],
167	            ))
168	        if record.get("terminated_round") == round_number and record.get("end_narration"):
169	            events.append(_memory_spec(
170	                record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility", "agent_only"),
171	                record.get("end_event_type", "fact_ended"), record["end_narration"],
172	            ))
173	    return events

176	def _memory_spec(holder, visibility, event_type, text):
177	    group_id = "community" if visibility == "public" else holder
178	    agent_id = None if holder == "community" else holder
179	    return {"event_type": event_type, "text": text, "agent_id": agent_id, "group_id": group_id}

182	def assign_role(
183	    role_name, agent_id, fluents, round_number, args=None,
184	    exclusive=False, narration=None, visibility="public", event_type="fact_initiated",
185	):
186	    """The default `args=None` (-> `[agent_id]`) is correct only for a role
187	    every eligible agent holds *simultaneously and independently* (e.g.
188	    "fisher" — one open record per agent, all coexisting on purpose).
189	
190	    For a role only one agent holds *at a time* (a rotating recorder,
191	    steward, monitor), pass `exclusive=True` instead of trying to get
192	    `args` right yourself — set_fact()'s own termination logic only closes
193	    a previous record when `(fluent_name, args)` matches exactly, so a
194	    plain `args=[agent_id]` for an exclusive role means each new holder's
195	    assignment uses different args than the last, never terminates the
196	    previous holder's record, and leaves multiple simultaneously-"open"
197	    holders for the same role — confirmed directly: `current_holder()`
198	    then returns whichever one happens to appear first in `fluents`,
199	    silently wrong the instant a rotation happens. `exclusive=True` forces
200	    a fixed `args=[]` regardless of whatever `args` was passed, making
201	    that mistake structurally unreachable through this parameter rather
202	    than something the caller has to remember to get right.
203

205	    visible, memory-worthy event (e.g. "Kai has become the pot keeper") —
206	    same contract as `set_fact()`, since this is just its role-shaped
207	    convenience wrapper; previously always silent (`narration=None`)."""
208	    resolved_args = [] if exclusive else (args if args is not None else [agent_id])
209	    return set_fact(
```

2:     for record in fluents:

7:             and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)

10:     return None

13: def current_holder(fluents, role_name, round_number):
14:     """The agent_id currently holding role_name, or None if unassigned.
15:     Unlike role_holder() above (which checks whether one *specific* agent
16:     holds a role — the question a fisher's own prompt needs to answer
17:     about itself), this answers "who holds it" without knowing who to ask
18:     first — the lookup an action needs when its own institution.json
19:     `actor_role` names a role but the specific agent rotates over rounds.
20:     Deliberately never cached anywhere (not in institution.json, not on
21:     any object) — this function, called fresh each time, is the single
22:     place "who currently holds this role" gets answered, so a rotation
23:     can never leave a second, stale answer sitting somewhere else. Relies
24:     on the same exclusivity every role fluent already has: one open
25:     record per role name at a time (set_fact()'s own termination-on-write
26:     behavior enforces this for role fluents the same as any other)."""
27:     for record in fluents:
28:         if (
29:             record["fluent"] == role_name
30:             and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
31:             and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
32:         ):
33:             return record["holder"]
34:     return None
35: 
36: 
37: def set_fact(
38:     fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
39:     narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
40: ):
41:     """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
42:     exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
43:     the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
44:     non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
45:     tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
46:     "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.
47: 
48:     `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
49:     (the same convention actions/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
50:     `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
51:     record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
52:     how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
53:     holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
54:     migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
55:     `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
56:     agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
57:     `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
58:     monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
59:     public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
60:     agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.
61: 
62:     Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
63:     layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
64:     picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
65:     entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
66:     fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
67:     `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).
68:     """
69:     for record in fluents:
70:         if (
71:             record["fluent"] == fluent_name
72:             and record["args"] == args
73:             and record["terminated_round"] is None
74:         ):
75:             record["terminated_round"] = round_number
76:     record = {
77:         "fluent": fluent_name,
78:         "args": args,
79:         "holder": holder,
80:         "initiated_round": round_number,
81:         "terminated_round": None,
82:     }
83:     if narration is not None:
84:         record["narration"] = narration
85:         record["visibility"] = visibility
86:         record["event_type"] = event_type
87:     fluents.append(record)
88:     return fluents
89: 
90: 
91: def end_fact(
92:     fluents, fluent_name, args, round_number,
93:     narration=None, visibility=None, event_type="fact_ended",
94: ):
95:     """Terminate the open record for (fluent_name, args), if any, without
96:     opening a replacement — e.g. a ban that's been served in full. Pass
97:     `narration` to describe the closing event itself (e.g. "Your ban has
98:     been lifted.") — same rules as `set_fact()`: reaches prompt (for
99:     exactly the round it closes, via `visible_facts()`) and memory
100:     automatically. `visibility` defaults to the record's own opening
101:     `visibility` if not given; only meaningful when `narration` is set."""
102:     for record in fluents:
103:         if (
104:             record["fluent"] == fluent_name
105:             and record["args"] == args
106:             and record["terminated_round"] is None
107:         ):
108:             record["terminated_round"] = round_number
109:             if narration is not None:
110:                 record["end_narration"] = narration
111:                 record["end_visibility"] = (
112:                     visibility if visibility is not None else record.get("visibility", "agent_only")
113:                 )
114:                 record["end_event_type"] = event_type
115:     return fluents
116: 
117: 
118: def _visible_to(agent_id, holder, visibility):
119:     return visibility == "public" or holder == agent_id
120: 
121: 
122: def visible_facts(fluents, agent_id, round_number):
123:     """Every fluent record with something narrated for right now and
124:     visible to agent_id — either public, or held by agent_id itself. Two
125:     cases: a currently-holdsAt record's opening `narration` (visible for
126:     as long as the fact stays open), and a record that closed exactly this
127:     round, surfaced via its `end_narration` for that one round only (the
128:     two are mutually exclusive per record: a record can't be both
129:     currently-open and closed-this-round). Used by the engine's prompt
130:     renderer to build an agent's "what's currently true" section; never
131:     interprets a raw value itself, only surfaces narration the mechanism
132:     that wrote the fact already authored."""
133:     results = []
134:     for record in fluents:
135:         if (
136:             record.get("narration")
137:             and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("visibility"))
138:             and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
139:             and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
140:         ):
141:             results.append(record)
142:         elif (
143:             record.get("terminated_round") == round_number
144:             and record.get("end_narration")
145:             and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility"))
146:         ):
147:             results.append({**record, "narration": record["end_narration"]})
148:     return results
149: 
150: 
151: def fact_memory_events(fluents, round_number):
152:     """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
153:     this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the
154:     shape `actions/*.py`'s `memory_writes()` already returns:
155:     `{event_type, text, agent_id, group_id}`). The caller
156:     (`engine/simulate.py`) turns these into actual `write_episode()` calls,
157:     once per round after all of that round's actions have run — not once
158:     per action, since a fact set by an early action would otherwise still
159:     read as "newly opened" to a later action's own call and get logged
160:     twice."""
161:     events = []
162:     for record in fluents:
163:         if record.get("initiated_round") == round_number and record.get("narration"):
164:             events.append(_memory_spec(
165:                 record["holder"], record.get("visibility", "agent_only"),
166:                 record.get("event_type", "fact_initiated"), record["narration"],
167:             ))
168:         if record.get("terminated_round") == round_number and record.get("end_narration"):
169:             events.append(_memory_spec(
170:                 record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility", "agent_only"),
171:                 record.get("end_event_type", "fact_ended"), record["end_narration"],
172:             ))
173:     return events
174: 
175: 
176: def _memory_spec(holder, visibility, event_type, text):
177:     group_id = "community" if visibility == "public" else holder
178:     agent_id = None if holder == "community" else holder
179:     return {"event_type": event_type, "text": text, "agent_id": agent_id, "group_id": group_id}
180: 
181: 
182: def assign_role(
183:     role_name, agent_id, fluents, round_number, args=None,
184:     exclusive=False, narration=None, visibility="public", event_type="fact_initiated",

def set_fact(
    fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
    narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
):
    """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
    exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
    the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
    non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
    tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
    "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.

    `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
    (the same convention actions/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
    `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
    record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
    how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
    holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
    migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
    `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
    agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
    `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
    monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
    public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
    agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.

    Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
    layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
    picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
    entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
    fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
    `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).

        if (
            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
            and record["args"] == args
            and record["terminated_round"] is None
        ):
            record["terminated_round"] = round_number
    record = {
        "fluent": fluent_name,
        "args": args,
        "holder": holder,
        "initiated_round": round_number,
        "terminated_round": None,
    }
    if narration is not None:
        record["narration"] = narration
        record["visibility"] = visibility
        record["event_type"] = event_type
    fluents.append(record)

    fluents, fluent_name, args, round_number,
    narration=None, visibility=None, event_type="fact_ended",
):

    opening a replacement — e.g. a ban that's been served in full. Pass
    `narration` to describe the closing event itself (e.g. "Your ban has
    been lifted.") — same rules as `set_fact()`: reaches prompt (for
    exactly the round it closes, via `visible_facts()`) and memory
    automatically. `visibility` defaults to the record's own opening
    `visibility` if not given; only meaningful when `narration` is set."""
    for record in fluents:

            record["fluent"] == fluent_name
            and record["args"] == args
            and record["terminated_round"] is None
        ):
            record["terminated_round"] = round_number
            if narration is not None:

                record["end_visibility"] = (

    return visibility == "public" or holder == agent_id


def visible_facts(fluents, agent_id, round_number):
    """Every fluent record with something narrated for right now and
    visible to agent_id — either public, or held by agent_id itself. Two
    cases: a currently-holdsAt record's opening `narration` (visible for
    as long as the fact stays open), and a record that closed exactly this
    round, surfaced via its `end_narration` for that one round only (the
    two are mutually exclusive per record: a record can't be both
    currently-open and closed-this-round). Used by the engine's prompt
    renderer to build an agent's "what's currently true" section; never
    interprets a raw value itself, only surfaces narration the mechanism
    that wrote the fact already authored."""
    results = []
    for record in fluents:
        if (
            record.get("narration")
            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("visibility"))
            and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
            and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
        ):
            results.append(record)
        elif (
            record.get("terminated_round") == round_number
            and record.get("end_narration")
            and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility"))

    """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
    this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the

    once per round after all of that round's actions have run — not once

37: def set_fact(
38:     fluents, fluent_name, args, holder, round_number,
39:     narration=None, visibility="agent_only", event_type="fact_initiated",
40: ):
41:     """General-purpose fluent write: terminate any open record for this
42:     exact (fluent_name, args) pair, then open a new one. assign_role() is
43:     the role-shaped special case of this (see below); use this directly for
44:     non-role facts — an obligation, a sanction, a status a norm wants
45:     tracked — where `holder` may be an individual agent_id or the sentinel
46:     "community" for a fact that isn't about one specific agent.
47: 
48:     `narration` is optional, already in-world-phrased plain language
49:     (the same convention actions/*.py's memory_writes() already uses for its
50:     `text` field) describing this fact for whoever it's visible to. A
51:     record with no narration renders nowhere — it's plumbing only (this is
52:     how plain role_fluent records, like the "fisher" role every agent
53:     holds, stay invisible to the notice renderer without needing a
54:     migration). `visibility` is `"public"` (surfaced to every agent) or
55:     `"agent_only"` (surfaced only when `holder` matches the requesting
56:     agent) — only meaningful when `narration` is set. Default to
57:     `"public"` for anything a community norm would plausibly want logged or
58:     monitored (this project's own adopted norms consistently call for
59:     public ledgers/monitors); use `"agent_only"` for something between one
60:     agent and the mechanism, like an individual warning.
61: 
62:     Whenever `narration` is set, the same text also reaches the memory
63:     layer automatically (see `fact_memory_events()` below) — `event_type`
64:     picks which of `engine/memory/write.py`'s `IMPORTANCE_BY_EVENT_TYPE`
65:     entries it's logged under; the generic `"fact_initiated"` default is
66:     fine unless a more specific existing type applies (e.g.
67:     `"graduated_sanction_applied"` for a real sanction).
68:     """

70:         if (
71:             record["fluent"] == fluent_name
72:             and record["args"] == args
73:             and record["terminated_round"] is None
74:         ):
75:             record["terminated_round"] = round_number
76:     record = {
77:         "fluent": fluent_name,
78:         "args": args,
79:         "holder": holder,
80:         "initiated_round": round_number,
81:         "terminated_round": None,
82:     }
83:     if narration is not None:
84:         record["narration"] = narration
85:         record["visibility"] = visibility
86:         record["event_type"] = event_type
87:     fluents.append(record)
88:     return fluents

91: def end_fact(
92:     fluents, fluent_name, args, round_number,
93:     narration=None, visibility=None, event_type="fact_ended",
94: ):
95:     """Terminate the open record for (fluent_name, args), if any, without
96:     opening a replacement — e.g. a ban that's been served in full. Pass
97:     `narration` to describe the closing event itself (e.g. "Your ban has
98:     been lifted.") — same rules as `set_fact()`: reaches prompt (for
99:     exactly the round it closes, via `visible_facts()`) and memory
100:     automatically. `visibility` defaults to the record's own opening
101:     `visibility` if not given; only meaningful when `narration` is set."""
102:     for record in fluents:
103:         if (
104:             record["fluent"] == fluent_name
105:             and record["args"] == args
106:             and record["terminated_round"] is None
107:         ):
108:             record["terminated_round"] = round_number
109:             if narration is not None:
110:                 record["end_narration"] = narration
111:                 record["end_visibility"] = (
112:                     visibility if visibility is not None else record.get("visibility", "agent_only")
113:                 )
114:                 record["end_event_type"] = event_type
115:     return fluents
116:

118: def _visible_to(agent_id, holder, visibility):
119:     return visibility == "public" or holder == agent_id
120:

122: def visible_facts(fluents, agent_id, round_number):
123:     """Every fluent record with something narrated for right now and
124:     visible to agent_id — either public, or held by agent_id itself. Two
125:     cases: a currently-holdsAt record's opening `narration` (visible for
126:     as long as the fact stays open), and a record that closed exactly this
127:     round, surfaced via its `end_narration` for that one round only (the
128:     two are mutually exclusive per record: a record can't be both
129:     currently-open and closed-this-round). Used by the engine's prompt
130:     renderer to build an agent's "what's currently true" section; never
131:     interprets a raw value itself, only surfaces narration the mechanism
132:     that wrote the fact already authored."""
133:     results = []
134:     for record in fluents:
135:         if (
136:             record.get("narration")
137:             and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("visibility"))
138:             and record["initiated_round"] <= round_number
139:             and (record["terminated_round"] is None or record["terminated_round"] > round_number)
140:         ):
141:             results.append(record)
142:         elif (
143:             record.get("terminated_round") == round_number
144:             and record.get("end_narration")
145:             and _visible_to(agent_id, record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility"))
146:         ):
147:             results.append({**record, "narration": record["end_narration"]})
148:     return results
149:

151: def fact_memory_events(fluents, round_number):
152:     """Memory-episode specs for every fact newly opened or newly closed
153:     this exact round that carries narration — pure, no I/O (mirrors the
154:     shape `actions/*.py`'s `memory_writes()` already returns:
155:     `{event_type, text, agent_id, group_id}`). The caller
156:     (`engine/simulate.py`) turns these into actual `write_episode()` calls,
157:     once per round after all of that round's actions have run — not once
158:     per action, since a fact set by an early action would otherwise still
159:     read as "newly opened" to a later action's own call and get logged
160:     twice."""
161:     events = []
162:     for record in fluents:
163:         if record.get("initiated_round") == round_number and record.get("narration"):
164:             events.append(_memory_spec(
165:                 record["holder"], record.get("visibility", "agent_only"),
166:                 record.get("event_type", "fact_initiated"), record["narration"],
167:             ))
168:         if record.get("terminated_round") == round_number and record.get("end_narration"):
169:             events.append(_memory_spec(
170:                 record["holder"], record.get("end_visibility", "agent_only"),
171:                 record.get("end_event_type", "fact_ended"), record["end_narration"],
172:             ))
173:     return events
174: 
175: 
176: def _memory_spec(holder, visibility, event_type, text):
177:     group_id = "community" if visibility == "public" else holder
178:     agent_id = None if holder == "community" else holder
179:     return {"event_type": event_type, "text": text, "agent_id": agent_id, "group_id": group_id}

182: def assign_role(
183:     role_name, agent_id, fluents, round_number, args=None,
184:     exclusive=False, narration=None, visibility="public", event_type="fact_initiated",
185: ):
186:     """The default `args=None` (-> `[agent_id]`) is correct only for a role
187:     every eligible agent holds *simultaneously and independently* (e.g.
188:     "fisher" — one open record per agent, all coexisting on purpose).
189: 
190:     For a role only one agent holds *at a time* (a rotating recorder,
191:     steward, monitor), pass `exclusive=True` instead of trying to get
192:     `args` right yourself — set_fact()'s own termination logic only closes
193:     a previous record when `(fluent_name, args)` matches exactly, so a
194:     plain `args=[agent_id]` for an exclusive role means each new holder's
195:     assignment uses different args than the last, never terminates the
196:     previous holder's record, and leaves multiple simultaneously-"open"
197:     holders for the same role — confirmed directly: `current_holder()`
198:     then returns whichever one happens to appear first in `fluents`,
199:     silently wrong the instant a rotation happens. `exclusive=True` forces
200:     a fixed `args=[]` regardless of whatever `args` was passed, making
201:     that mistake structurally unreachable through this parameter rather
202:     than something the caller has to remember to get right.
203: 
204:     `narration`/`visibility`/`event_type` let a role grant also be a
205:     visible, memory-worthy event (e.g. "Kai has become the pot keeper") —
206:     same contract as `set_fact()`, since this is just its role-shaped
207:     convenience wrapper; previously always silent (`narration=None`)."""
208:     resolved_args = [] if exclusive else (args if args is not None else [agent_id])
209:     return set_fact(
210:         fluents, role_name, resolved_args, agent_id, round_number,
211:         narration=narration, visibility=visibility, event_type=event_type,
212:     )

```python
1	"""Fixed simulation physics — never editable by the norm-implementer,
2	regardless of what any norm asks for. Ported directly from Gupta et al.'s
3	CPR-game codebase (Codes/Gupta/CPRG_fishing, branch origin/hiromu/llm-norm,
4	ostrom3/Agent.py and Model.py), not this project's own design — a norm can
5	change caps, deposits, bans, and schedules (all implementer-owned, in
6	actions/rules/ and actions/), but the underlying catch equation, regrowth
7	rate, and survival economics below are the fixed rules of the world those
8	choices play out against, not something a community vote should be able
9	to rewrite.
10	
11	Lives under engine/ specifically so it's outside the norm-implementer's
12	permission.edit allowlist (actions/rules/*/*, actions/*, prompts/*, plus a
13	few named files) by construction, the same way engine/simulate.py and
14	engine/llm_agents.py already are. The rate constants below live here for
15	the same reason the equations do, not in state/config.json (which the
16	norm-implementer can freely edit) — a fixed formula reading a
17	norm-implementer-editable rate is exactly as rewritable as the formula
18	itself would be.
19	
20	`available_stock()` moved in from the old `mechanisms/stock_check.py`
21	(2026-09-09, when `mechanisms/` was renamed to `roles/` and reserved for
22	role/fluent code only) — it's a trivial one-line accessor, but it's fixed
23	protected infrastructure exactly like everything else here, not
24	role-related, so it belongs next to the physics it reads alongside.
25	"""
26	
27	HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY = 0.05  # catchability coefficient q in catch_from_effort()
28	GROWTH_RATE = 0.2  # logistic growth rate in apply_regrowth()
29	CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG = 300  # lake's ceiling, also its starting stock
30	CONSUMPTION_KG = 1.0  # fixed per-round cost every fisher owes just to get by
31	
32	
33	def catch_from_effort(effort, stock_kg):
34	    """Linear Schaefer-style catch equation (catch = effort x stock x
35	    catchability), matching Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest(). effort is
36	    the agent's own [0.0, 1.0] fishing-intensity choice; HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
37	    is their catchability coefficient q."""
38	    return effort * stock_kg * HARVEST_PRODUCTIVITY
39	
40	
41	def apply_regrowth(stock_kg):
42	    """Logistic growth on the leftover (post-harvest) stock — matches
43	    Gupta et al.'s CPRModel.step():
44	    ΔR = growth_rate * R * (1 - R/capacity), applied to what's left after
45	    harvest, not a flat per-round add. Growth slows as the stock nears
46	    carrying capacity and (unlike a flat add) can't outrun a depleted lake."""
47	    grown = stock_kg + GROWTH_RATE * stock_kg * (1 - stock_kg / CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
48	    return min(grown, CARRYING_CAPACITY_KG)
49	
50	
51	def apply_consumption(payoff, harvested_kg):
52	    """Running per-agent balance: this trip's catch in, the fixed
53	    consumption cost out — matches Gupta et al.'s CPRAgent.harvest():
54	    self.payoff += harvest_amount; self.payoff -= self.model.consumption.
55	    Unlike catch/regrowth this isn't about the lake at all — it's whether
56	    a fisher can keep feeding themselves from what they bring in."""
57	    return payoff + harvested_kg - CONSUMPTION_KG
58	
59	
60	def is_dead(payoff):
61	    """Matches Gupta et al.'s `if self.payoff < 0: self.dead = True` —
62	    permanent once true; nothing in this project ever resurrects an agent."""
63	    return payoff < 0
64	
65	
66	def alive_agent_ids(agents, runtime):
67	    """The agent_id iteration order every action should use, not
68	    state["agents"] directly — excludes anyone in runtime["dead_agents"].
69	    One shared helper so death exclusion can't be forgotten by an action
70	    rewrite the way a hand-rolled check per action could be."""
71	    dead = set(runtime.get("dead_agents", []))
72	    return [agent_id for agent_id in agents if agent_id not in dead]
73	
74	
75	def available_stock(runtime):
76	    return runtime["stock_kg"]
```
